title: Protocol for identification of airborne asbestos fibres in the urban areas and spatio-temporal trend
author: Hajizadeh, Jafari, et al.

steps.title: Prepare MCE filter (BS ISO14966)
steps.instruction: Prepare mixed cellulose ester (MCE) filters according to British Standard ISO 14966 before sampling air for asbestos analysis.

steps.title: Fix sample on holder with adhesive
steps.instruction: After sampling, fix the filter onto an SEM holder using double‑sided adhesive.

steps.title: Gold coat filter (~100 Å) in vacuum coater
steps.instruction: Place the adhesive‑fixed holder in an EMITECH K450X vacuum coating apparatus (England) and deposit a gold layer of approximately 100 Å thickness on the filter surface.

steps.title: Image filter by SEM at ≥2000×
steps.instruction: Insert the gold‑coated filter into a scanning electron microscope (SEM, model WEGA/TESCAN, Czech Republic) and examine virtually the entire graticule area of the filter at a magnification of 2000× or higher.

steps.title: Identify asbestos fibres by size criteria
steps.instruction: Record all fibres that meet the following specifications: length greater than 5 μm, diameter less than 3 μm, and a length‑to‑diameter ratio of at least 3 : 1; classify these as asbestos fibres.

steps.title: Validate counts with repeat SEM analysis
steps.instruction: To confirm accuracy, analyse the same sample three times on a second SEM instrument under identical conditions and verify that results do not differ significantly (p < 0.05).

steps.title: Perform EDX to determine fibre composition
steps.instruction: Couple an energy‑dispersive X‑ray (EDX) system to the SEM and acquire elemental spectra for each counted fibre to distinguish asbestos fibres from non‑asbestos fibres.

steps.title: Calculate fibre concentration using SEM equation
steps.instruction: Compute the concentration of asbestos fibres (C_SEM, fibres · ml⁻¹) with the equation C_SEM = 1000 N A V n a, where N = number of fibres counted, A = effective collecting area of filter (≈ 385 mm²), V = volume of air sampled (L), n = number of fields (photos) counted, and a = calibrated surface area (mm²).
